title: Punctuation and commands
goal: Marks, capitals and editing keys are pinned before any word is, so a word can never take their strokes.

blocks.x: Punctuation, commands and fingerspelling are reserved ahead of every word. A word that wanted a reserved stroke moves to its next-cheapest outline. The upside: these strokes are the same wherever you are.
Every mark has exactly one stroke, and so does every command. A mark that spaces differently (the hyphen that joins words, the one with a space round it) is a different mark with a stroke of its own.

[[KPA]] capitalises the next word and keeps the space; [[KPA*]] does the same glued to the word before. That is how names are handled: a name types as its ordinary sound-alike outline, capitalised by this stroke first. The shortcut is the name lane: strike `#` alone (it types nothing) and then the same outline, and the name comes out capitalised (`#`, then `TKAPBL` is *Daniel*); a name the dictionary lacks is read from names alone ([the name lane](#/ref/names)).
Add the star to a movement stroke to **select** while you move: [[STPH*R]] is Shift+Left. `STPH` is the family; the right-hand keys say which direction.

The movement strokes and Backspace go the moment the **first** key comes up, not the last, so you can **hold** `STPH` and tap `-R`, `-R`, `-R` to walk the cursor left, then tap `-P` to go up, with no lifting in between. This needs Keymux; the [reference page](#/ref/punctuation/send-on-the-first-key-up) has the full list and the one trap.
F1 to F12 are `TPW` plus the number's own sound: [[TPWUPB]] is F1, [[TPWO]] is F2.
